title: B2+ · L17 — Phrasal verbs (negotiation)
description: Phrasal verbs de negociacion: give in, hold out, meet halfway, back down, walk away, y otros.

questions.prompt: Negociacion de contrato dura 8 horas. Al final, el otro lado cede: 'They finally gave in on the pricing.'
questions.question: 'After hours of debate, they finally gave in' means:
questions.explanation: 'Give in' = ceder, capitular tras resistencia. Central en vocabulario de negociacion. Connotacion: implica cesion involuntaria (contra tu preferencia inicial). 'Don't give in on X' es mantra de negociation coaching. Diferencia con 'cave in' (mas fuerte, sugiere colapso ante presion) y 'meet halfway' (compromise mutuo, no cesion unilateral). Registro: neutro. Error hispano: interpretar como 'entregar/handing in' — es el opuesto psicologico (rendirse).
examples: Don't give in on the base salary — hold your ground even if it takes weeks. → coaching mode
After lengthy discussion, the seller gave in on the price and dropped 15%. → business report

questions.prompt: Tu equipo esta pensando aceptar la primera oferta. Le dices: 'We're going to hold out for a better offer.'
questions.question: 'We're going to hold out for a better offer' means:
options: Wait / resist to get better terms.
questions.explanation: 'Hold out' = resistir/esperar esperando terminos mejores. Opuesto psicologico exacto de 'give in'. Estrategia valida cuando tienes leverage (opciones alternativas, tiempo, urgencia inversa). Colocacion nativa: 'hold out for X' (esperar X — mejor oferta, mejor precio). Se usa en negociacion salarial ('hold out for six figures'), inmobiliaria ('hold out for a cash offer'), M&A. Registro: business y personal. Error hispano: interpretar 'hold' literal = agarrar/sujetar.
examples: We held out for six months and got 30% more than the initial offer. → paciencia paga
The union held out until wages were increased across the board. → contexto laboral

questions.statement: 'To meet halfway' means both sides make concessions to reach agreement.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Meet halfway' = encontrarse en el medio con concesiones mutuas — simbolo cristalizado del compromise en negociacion. Metafora fisica: dos personas caminan una hacia la otra y se encuentran a mitad del camino. Distinto de 'give in' (unilateral) o 'cave in' (bajo presion). Uso literal ('let's meet halfway between our offices') y figurativo ('meet in the middle on price'). Registro: neutro-collaborative. Colocacion asociada: 'find a middle ground' (equivalente).
examples: Let's meet halfway on the price — 550 instead of your 500 or my 600. → resolucion aritmetica
If they're willing to meet us halfway on scope, we have a deal. → colaboracion condicionada

questions.prompt: Un politico defendia una postura firme. Bajo presion mediatica cede: 'She backed down under pressure.'
questions.question: 'She backed down under pressure' means:
options: Retreated from a position / stopped insisting.
questions.explanation: 'Back down' = retroceder de una postura, retirarse. Puede ser sabio (dato nuevo) o debil (miedo) segun contexto. Opuesto exacto: 'stand firm' o 'hold your ground'. Colocaciones nativas: 'refuse to back down' (rechazar retroceder — postura firme), 'back down under pressure' (con presion). Diferencia sutil con 'back off' (retroceder fisica o psicologicamente para dar espacio) y 'back out' (retirarse de compromiso).
examples: He refused to back down despite intense scrutiny from the press. → firmeza politica
The company backed down after public outcry over the policy change. → capitulacion corporativa

questions.text: If they won't budge on the terms, we should be prepared to walk away from the deal.
questions.explanation: Frase clave de negociacion — invoca BATNA (Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — la mejor alternativa si no hay acuerdo). Fenomeno de connected speech: 'won't budge' con /ntb/ cluster reducido /wəʊnˈbʌdʒ/; 'walk away' con /kə/ enlazado /wɔːkəˈweɪ/. Vocabulario: 'budge' = moverse minimamente (verbo), muy usado en negativa; 'walk away' = abandonar sin cerrar deal. La disposicion a walk away ES tu mayor leverage — es la ensenanza central de 'Getting to Yes'. Registro: business y personal.
examples: They wouldn't budge on the delivery date, so we walked away and went with a competitor.
The best leverage in any negotiation is being ready to walk away with confidence.

questions.prompt: Contratos finales de una adquisicion. El CEO dice: 'Let's hammer out the final terms tonight.'
questions.question: 'Let's hammer out the final terms' means:
questions.explanation: 'Hammer out' = trabajar/negociar los detalles hasta acordar y finalizar. Metafora de herreria: forjar el metal a golpes hasta que toma forma exacta — sugiere esfuerzo intenso y iterativo. Muy comun en contratos, deals de M&A, acuerdos sindicales, tratados internacionales. Colocaciones nativas: 'hammer out an agreement', 'hammer out the details', 'hammer out a compromise'. Registro: business y politico. Sugiere trabajo duro, no facil.
examples: The lawyers spent all night hammering out the acquisition terms before market open.
We'll hammer out the details Monday morning over coffee. → registro casual

questions.prompt: Empareja cada phrasal verb de negociacion con su traduccion:
questions.explanation: Set completo de phrasal verbs esenciales de negociacion. Distinciones sutiles pero importantes: 'give in' (ceder tras resistencia — puede ser voluntario); 'cave in' (colapsar bajo presion — connota debilidad, mas fuerte); 'back down' (retirar postura — puede ser sabio); 'walk away' (abandonar todo — leverage maximo); 'hold out' (esperar mejor); 'meet halfway' (compromise mutuo). Registro: todos business y personal.
examples: The board caved in to shareholder demands after weeks of pressure. → connotacion negativa
Don't cave in on the equity — it's your leverage for future rounds. → coaching negociacion

questions.target: We can meet you halfway on price, but we're not willing to back down on the delivery timeline.
questions.explanation: Estrategia de negociador senior: concede en un area de baja prioridad (price), mantiene firme en area de alta prioridad (timeline). Formula profesional de balance que evita el 'winner takes all' y demuestra flexibilidad calibrada. 'Willing to back down' vs 'give in' — 'back down' es mas suave y elegante para expresar apertura. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'price,', enfasis en 'not willing' y 'timeline'. Contracciones: 'we're' obligatoria. Registro: business negotiation profesional.
examples: Happy to meet halfway on scope, but we won't budge on quality — that's non-negotiable.
We can back off on the volume ask, but the price has to stand as offered. → alternate structure

questions.prompt: Cuenta como tomaste una decision arriesgada: 'She talked me into taking the leap.'
questions.question: 'They talked us into signing' means:
questions.explanation: 'Talk into' = convencer/persuadir a hacer algo. Colocacion: 'talk someone into + gerund'. Opuesto: 'talk out of' = disuadir. Muy usado en contextos de vendedores, negociadores, familia, amigos. Connotacion: sugiere persuasion activa (no manipulacion necesariamente). 'Take the leap' = dar el salto (metafora de compromiso arriesgado). Registro: neutro, todos contextos. Error hispano: 'talk with' o 'talk to' son distintos — 'talk into' requiere el sentido persuasivo.
examples: She talked me into taking the leap and starting my own business. → decision de vida
My mom talked me out of quitting too early — best advice I ever got. → opuesto (disuadir)

questions.statement: 'To bring someone around' means to persuade them to change their view.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Bring around' = convencer a alguien de cambiar de opinion, tipicamente con paciencia y evidencia. Metafora fisica: hacer que alguien 'venga' hacia tu vista, girandolo. Comun en negociacion, ventas, politica, family dynamics. Colocaciones: 'bring the board around', 'bring the skeptics around', 'took months to bring him around'. Distinto de 'bring up' (mencionar tema) y 'bring about' (causar). Registro: neutro-professional. Suele implicar proceso, no persuasion instantanea.
examples: It took months, but we finally brought him around to the new approach. → proceso largo
Data and a live demo brought the skeptics around by the end of the quarter. → medios de persuasion

questions.prompt: Negocias con un vendedor de coche. Te dicen: 'The seller wouldn't come down on the price.'
questions.question: 'The seller wouldn't come down on the price' means:
questions.explanation: 'Come down on price' = bajar el precio. Muy comun en negociacion comercial (coches, casas, servicios). Opuesto: 'go up on'. Colocaciones nativas: 'come down on X (amount/percentage)', 'come down to Y (final number)'. Uso literal y coloquial. Alternativas: 'drop the price', 'lower the price'. Registro: casual-professional negotiation. Error hispano: interpretar literal como movimiento fisico descendente.
examples: Would you come down on price if we paid cash upfront? → apalancar cash
They came down 10% after we mentioned competing offers. → uso de leverage

questions.text: We're not going to nickel-and-dime this — let's just close it out and move on to the next round.
questions.explanation: Discurso ejecutivo maduro. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'we're not going to' se reduce a /wɪəˈnɒtɡʌnə/; 'close it out' con catenacion /kləʊzɪˈtaʊt/; 'move on' con /vɒ/ /muːvɒn/. Vocabulario C1 senior: 'nickel-and-dime' = regatear obsesivamente por cantidades pequenas (metafora de moneditas — 5 y 10 centavos US); 'close out' = cerrar/finalizar formalmente; 'move on to' = pasar a. Uso: cuando quieres priorizar velocidad y relacion sobre optimizar cada centavo. Registro: business ejecutivo.
examples: Let's not nickel-and-dime — the long-term relationship is worth way more.
Time to close this out and focus on execution. → pivot de negociacion a implementacion

questions.prompt: Deal casi cerrado. El comprador se retira: 'They pulled out of the deal at the last minute.'
questions.question: 'They pulled out of the deal at the last minute' means:
questions.explanation: 'Pull out of' = retirarse formalmente (deal, contract, negotiation, competition). Diferencia con 'walk away' — pull out es mas formal y a menudo despues de commitment inicial o due diligence; walk away es mas al principio o durante. Registro: business/legal formal. Colocaciones: 'pulled out of the deal', 'pulled out of the race', 'pulled out of the market'. Error hispano: no confundir con 'pull off' (lograr algo dificil) — significado opuesto.
examples: The buyer pulled out three days before closing citing financing issues.
They pulled out of the partnership citing strategic changes at the board level.

questions.statement: 'To lay out' the terms means to present them clearly and thoroughly.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Lay out' = presentar de forma ordenada, detallada, sistemica. Metafora fisica: como poner papeles ordenados sobre una mesa para que el otro los vea todos. Muy usado en propuestas, presentaciones, planes estrategicos, contratos. Colocaciones: 'lay out the plan', 'lay out the options', 'lay out my thinking'. Registro: neutro-professional. Diferencia con 'lay off' (despedir empleados) — palabras homofonas pero significados totalmente distintos.
examples: The consultant laid out three options for us, each with pros and cons clearly detailed.
Let me lay out the plan before we discuss trade-offs and prioritization. → orden estructurado

questions.target: Here's where I'll hold out — I'm happy to meet you halfway on scope, but I won't cave in on the timeline.
questions.explanation: Estrategia magistral de negociador senior: hold out en X (posicion firme), meet halfway en Y (concesion calibrada), no cave in en Z (linea roja). Muestra dominio del set completo de phrasal verbs de negociacion y su distinct connotation. 'Cave in' es la palabra mas potente aqui — comunica que no vas a colapsar bajo presion. Ritmo natural: pausa marcada tras 'hold out —', tono firme creciente en 'won't cave in'. Contracciones: 'I'll', 'I'm', 'won't' obligatorias. Registro: negociation senior/staff level.
examples: I'll meet you halfway on price, but I'm holding out on payment terms — we need 30 days.
We can back off scope, but we're not caving on quality standards. → paired distincion
